ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, as amended, Articles 2, 5-2, 5-3 and 5-4, together with its Enforcement Decree; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Identification of Financial Transactions and Keeping Supporting Records for Beneficial Owners; Korean Commercial Act, as amended; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Registration of Non-Contentious Procedures Rules; Maritime Security and Marine Transportation Business Act; Financial Action Task Force Recommendations and KOFIU/FSC AML/CFT guidance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registration Office / Local District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) District Court Registry issues a certified certificate of company registration; (2) if required, a Korean notary public certifies the registrar's signature; (3) the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea affixes the Apostille. For non-Hague destination states, substitute step (3) with MOFA legalization and then consular legalization by the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing equivalent (Certificate of Corporate Registration Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registration Office / Local District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) Registry issues the current corporate registration certificate; (2) Korean notary authentication if requested by the receiving authority; (3) Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For non-Apostille countries, use MOFA authentication plus destination-state consular legalization only. Do not combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, district tax office in the jurisdiction of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) the tax office issues the business registration certificate; (2) where the receiving bank or registry requires a notarial layer, a Korean notary public certifies the authorized officer's signature; (3) the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the Apostille. For a non-Hague jurisdiction, carry out MOFA legalization followed by consular legalization at the destination diplomatic mission; never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public executing a power of attorney in the name of the founding shareholders and directors of the proposed Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) the power of attorney is executed in Korean or English and notarized by a Korean notary; (2) the Ministry of Foreign Affairs affixes an Apostille. In countries not party to the Apostille Convention, the notarized document must be authenticated by MOFA and then legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country. The two paths are mutually exclusive alternatives and cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy or notarized founding instrument)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and, after registration, the Local District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) notarize the Articles of Association before a Korean notary; (2) file for and obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For a non-Hague state, the notarized articles must go through MOFA legalization and then consular legalization at the destination consulate. Apostille and consular legalization must never be applied to the same document sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the escrow and operating account relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean branch of the global commercial bank selected for the offshore towage and salvage payment rail, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) the bank issues the reference letter on its letterhead; (2) a Korean notary certifies the bank officer's signature and corporate capacity; (3) the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the Apostille. For a destination state not in the Apostille Convention, use MOFA authentication and consular legalization by the destination embassy/consulate only; the two pathways are parallel and mutually exclusive and shall not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO at or above 25 percent, director, statutory officer, signatory, charterer, vessel owner, agent and material payment counterparty must be screened before incorporation through an enhanced due diligence workflow. Automated and human screening must cover OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU and UK autonomous sanctions, Korean FIU/KOFIU domestic blacklists, FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions, and the Korean Government's restrictive trade and defense lists. Because the business uses Lloyd's standard-form wires and escrow, every wire counterparty, IMO vessel number, flag state, P&I club, hull insurer, salvors and tug operator must also be screened for sanctions, terrorist-financing and maritime crime alerts. Politically exposed person status of shareholders and directors, including family members and close associates, must be determined through a Korean-licensed PEP database and must trigger source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification plus senior-management approval. Adverse media checks must cover maritime piracy, smuggling, illegal fishing, North Korea-related trafficking, sanctions evasion, bribery and fraud. Any red flag that remains unresolved must be escalated and, if not cleared, the engagement must be refused or reported to KOFIU as a suspicious transaction. Documentation of screening results must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS), operated by the Supreme Court Registration Division, together with the Korean Commercial Act company-name clearance rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name of a Korean Chusik Hoesa must be stated in Hangul. A foreign-language or romanized trade name may be included in the Articles of Association and used commercially only as a secondary name, while the Hangul registered name remains controlling for Korean public law and registration purposes. Foreign terms and brand names are transliterated phonetically into Hangul, and names having the same pronunciation as an existing legal name in the same registration jurisdiction are treated as confusingly similar and rejected. The four-tier naming convention applied by the registry is: (1) distinctive word or brand element; (2) business purpose descriptor; (3) indication of business type; and (4) the statutory liability suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. The registry will also reject an English transliteration that is phonetically identical to a protected or already-registered Korean name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If IROS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the registration judge of the competent District Court

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, December 20, 1962, as amended, including Article 289 on incorporation of a stock corporation, Article 290 on contents of the Articles of Incorporation, Article 292 on notarial certification of articles, Article 295 on share subscription, Article 305 on payment of subscription price, and Article 313 on registration of incorporation with the Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Korean District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operated under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea; for Seoul-registered entities, the filing window is the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital payment deposit certificate, director consent forms, and corporate seal documentation; upon approval the court issues the Certificate of Corporate Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None as to a minimum statutory paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. However, the full subscription price for the issued shares must be paid in before the incorporation registration application is submitted, and the payment must be made through a designated Korean bank and evidenced by a bank-issued capital payment deposit certificate. Funds are effectively unavailable for withdrawal to the corporate treasury until the Commercial Registry registration is completed; there is no separate post-registration escrow lockbox requirement for a general service corporation, but banks may apply enhanced due diligence and restricted disbursement procedures for a maritime towage and salvage entity classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF ___ CHUSIK HOESA. The undersigned constitute the first board of directors of the above-named stock corporation formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. The meeting was duly convened and held at Seoul, Republic of Korea, on ____. All initial directors were present in person or validly represented, quorum was continuously satisfied, and the chair was unanimously elected. It was resolved as follows. ONE: Ratification of Incorporation: All actions taken by the promoters, subscribers, and legal counsel in preparing and notarizing the Articles of Incorporation, opening the capital subscription bank account, and negotiating the towage and salvage business contracts are approved, ratified, and confirmed in every respect. TWO: Share Capital Subscription: The Board approves the issued share capital and the list of subscribers as recorded in the share subscription certificate; the paid-in capital has been or will immediately be deposited in full at the designated Korean bank. The representative director is directed to collect the capital payment deposit certificate and to complete all Korean Commercial Registry filings without delay. THREE: Registered Office: The registered office is established at the address listed in the Articles of Incorporation and at such additional operating offices as may be lawfully maintained. The representative director and any one other director are authorized to execute a lease or sublease, register the address, and place corporate signs and required notices at that office. FOUR: Banking Authorization: The Board authorizes the opening of corporate operating accounts at a Korean commercial bank. The authorized signatories shall be the representative director and the finance director; any two authorized signatories acting together may sign for instruments above fifty thousand United States dollars, and any one authorized signatory may sign for routine operating amounts. The accounts may receive funds by Lloyds Standard Form Wire and escrow payment rails, subject to the bank's anti-money laundering, know-your-client, and sanctions screening requirements. FIVE: Statutory Officer Appointments: The Board appoints the individuals named in the consent forms to serve as director, representative director, and statutory auditor. The auditor shall review the corporation's capital payment, accounting records, and treasury operations in accordance with the Commercial Act audit and inspection requirements. SIX: Compliance and Delegation: The Board adopts the corporate governance and anti-money laundering compliance manual, appoints the compliance officer, and authorizes the representative director to file all applications with the Commercial Registry, National Tax Service, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Korea Coast Guard, National Fire Agency, and any other competent public authority. All resolutions are effective immediately and may be relied upon by governmental authorities, banks, classification societies, insurers, and contracting counterparts. This certified resolution remains in force until duly amended by the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the Republic of Korea, acting under the Commercial Act and the Notary Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the full articles of incorporation in the Korean commercial registry form. The articles must state the company name ending in Chusik Hoesa, principal registered office address, the express corporate object of deep-sea tugboat towage, maritime emergency rescue, vessel and cargo salvage, wreck removal, offshore assistance contracts, and all related maritime support services. Define the number of authorized shares, par value, classes, methods of notice, duration, and the first directors. Have every promoter sign and affix a seal. Then submit the executed articles to a Korean notary public because, under Article 292 of the Commercial Act, un-notarized articles are ineffective for registration. Foreign promoters must provide legalized passports and certified Korean translations. The notary must certify the deed and return a certified original for filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or ID copies for all promoters and initial directors
Legalized or apostilled foreign corporate or personal documents
Power of attorney for any local formation agent
Consent forms of initial directors
Certified Korean translations of non-Korean documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query on corporate object, capital, or promoter authority, cure the deficiency by amending the relevant articles, obtaining fresh signatures, and re-executing the notarial deed. No emergency remedy exists because un-notarized articles are invalid; the registration application must be suspended until a fully notarized version is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription, Capital Payment, and Bank-Issued Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Korean commercial bank selected by the promoters and operating the capital deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Promoters of a Chusik Hoesa must make a written share subscription before payment is made. The subscription certificate must identify the proposed corporate name, the class and number of shares, subscription price, and subscriber address. Each promoter must deposit the full subscription price into a designated Korean bank account opened in the name of the corporation or in an escrow-like promoter subscription account if the bank requires it. The bank will issue a capital payment deposit certificate evidencing receipt of funds and the identity of the payers. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the later court registration application. Funds cannot be released before incorporation registration. If vessels, tugs, or salvage equipment are contributed as in-kind capital, retain a court-appointed appraiser report. For a Medium-Risk Enhanced maritime salvage corporate profile, the bank will also require source of wealth declarations, AML/KYC forms, and a description of towing and salvage counterparties.
required_dossiers: Written share subscription certificates
Capital payment deposit certificate issued by the designated bank
Bank AML/KYC account opening forms
Source of funds declarations and supporting documents
Valuation report and court approval for any in-kind capital contributions
Power of attorney for bank submissions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, supplement the file with certified financial statements, bank statements, or tax records. If the bank refuses the deposit, select another authorized Korean bank and re-deposit so the final certificate name and account fully match the corporate registration application; release of subscription funds before registration remains prohibited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration Application at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, accessed through the Korean Supreme Court e-registration service or directly at the registry window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registration application must be submitted to the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. In Korea this is managed by the Supreme Court Registry; for Seoul companies, the filing location is the Seoul Central District Court. The application must be signed by the initial directors and promoters or an authorized administrative agent. Attach the notarized articles, the capital payment certificate, signed director consent and appointment certificates, corporate seal certificate, and proof of payment of registration tax and local education tax. The registry verifies that the corporate name is distinguishable, the purpose is lawful, capital has been paid, and director and auditor consents are genuine. Upon approval the court makes the registration entry and issues a certified Corporate Registration Certificate. The company is deemed fully incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa at that moment; after registration, obtain certified extracts and use them for banking, tax, and maritime licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Completed Commercial Registration Application Form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment deposit certificate
Certificate of appointment or consent of each director and auditor
Corporate seal impression certificate
Registration tax and local education tax payment receipts
Power of attorney if filed by a local administrative agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure all omissions within the statutory correction period by submitting supplementary documents, corrected signatures, or revised notarized pages. If the corporate name is rejected as confusingly similar, adopt a new name by a board or promoter resolution, notarize the amendment, and refile. A denial can be challenged by objection to the Me?

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Bank Account, Tax Registration, and Statutory Corporate Governance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal and the local municipal tax office; Korean commercial bank for the permanent corporate account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of registration is issued, the representative director must complete post-incorporation statutory formalities. Open the permanent operating bank account with the registered commercial bank, providing the registration certificate and a board resolution setting signing authorities. File a corporate tax and business registration with the National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal, identify the statutory tax office for the registered address, and apply for an electronic tax invoice authentication certificate. Register the workplace with the local tax office, issue a corporate seal certificate, and file beneficial ownership information if requested under the Korean anti-money laundering framework. If the company will employ seafarers or shore staff, open the mandatory workers compensation, employment insurance, national pension, and health insurance accounts. Authorize the finance officer to operate Lloyds Standard Form Wire and escrow payment rails only after the bank has completed enhanced due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration
Corporate seal certificate
Articles of Incorporation and Board Resolution approving bank signatories
AML/Beneficial Ownership Disclosure forms
NT Tax business registration application and electronic tax invoice application
Office lease or registered address evidence
Workplace registration forms for labor and social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service rejects the business registration application, correct the data in HomeTax and resubmit. If the bank blocks the operating account due to AML concerns, provide charter parties, towage contracts, and customer due diligence files, or amend the Board Resolution to name additional signatories. Tax registry errors can be cured through a written correction request to the district tax office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Industrial License, Environmental Compliance, and Civil Defense Fire Safety Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Korea Coast Guard, National Fire Agency, and local port authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The business is a marine service operation rather than a factory, so no manufacturing operating license under the Korean Industrial Development Act applies. However, the vessel towage and salvage service itself is regulated by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and must be licensed before commencement. File the Marine Transportation Business License application for tugboat towage and salvage, including proof of financial soundness, vessel availability, crew licenses, and safety management systems. For any onshore office, jetty, workshop, or store, obtain a fire-fighting systems completion certificate from the National Fire Agency and a civil defense evacuation and emergency response plan. Submit marine environmental compliance to the Korea Coast Guard: oil pollution emergency plan, ballast water management plan, and waste handling logs. Portside facilities must have structural load inspections and dangerous substances handling clearance under the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Dangerous Substances Safety Management Act.
required_dossiers: Marine Transportation Business License application for towage and salvage
Certificate of Corporate Registration
Vessel ownership or bareboat charter certificate
Korean Register class certificate and safety management certificate
Crew license and seafarer employment records
Fire-fighting systems completion certificate for shore facility
Oil pollution emergency response plan and ballast water management plan
Civil defense plan and workplace safety registration
Structural load inspection report for piers or workshops
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries suspends or queries the license application, submit corrected financial statements, towage capability evidence, or crew qualification documents. If the Korea Coast Guard rejects the environmental plans, revise the emergency response procedures and reapply. Fire safety and structural defects must be corrected before the fire authority will issue the completion certificate; administrative appeal may be filed under the relevant Korean administrative procedure statutes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Maritime Transport Business Licensing Division; Korea Coast Guard for vessel safety, marine pollution, and oil spill response; National Fire Agency for shore facility fire safety and civil defense clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Transportation Support Business License for Tugboat Towage and Maritime Salvage, issued under the Korean Marine Transportation Act along with the Korea Coast Guard Operational Safety Approval and vessel-class certification by a recognized Korean classification society

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division, coordinated with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and Korea Coast Guard for marine-area environmental compliance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable as a Full EIA because a pure vessel towage and salvage operation creates no fixed industrial installation. The operation is subject to environmental registration under the Marine Environment Management Act, including waste handling, oil spill response, and ballast water management. If the company constructs a shore base, workshop, berth, or repair yard, the project will be classified as a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment project; if port-related construction exceeds the statutory EIA threshold under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, a Full EIA report will be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All machinery-space oily water must pass through a 15 ppm oil-water separator and any permitted discharge must not exceed 15 ppm oil content under MARPOL Annex I. Treated or macerated sewage may be discharged only beyond three nautical miles from the nearest land or in accordance with the vessel sewage treatment standard; raw sewage discharge beyond twelve nautical miles. Plastic discharge into the sea is strictly prohibited, and all garbage must be logged and delivered to port reception facilities. Ballast water management must meet the IMO D-2 standard of fewer than ten viable organisms per cubic meter for the specified organism classes. Hazardous wastes, including batteries, oil filters, and contaminated rags, must be segregated, labeled, stored under the Korean Waste Control Act, and consigned only to licensed hazardous waste treatment facilities. Bunkering operations must use controlled spill prevention equipment, and VOC emissions from fuel transfer must be minimized or recovered where a vapor recovery connection is required by Korean air quality regulations; marine fuel sulfur content must not exceed 0.50 percent m/m under MARPOL Annex VI, with stricter 0.10 percent m/m sulfur limits in challenged port air-quality control areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For all onshore premises, obtain the Fire-Fighting Systems Completion Certificate under the Fire Prevention, Installation and Maintenance of Fire-Fighting Systems Act, the Civil Defense Act emergency evacuation and response plan approval, and the workplace commencement report under the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act. Piers, gangways, workshops, and office floors must pass structural load inspection and electrical and gas safety inspection before operation. If any dangerous substances, such as marine fuels, lubricants, or chemical salvage agents, are stored

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, 90 Gajeong-ro, Yuseong-gu, Daejeon; online portal HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export and customs declarations are processed with Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first determine whether it has a domestic place of business in Korea under the Value-Added Tax Act. If it maintains a branch, fixed office, vessel operating base, or other permanent establishment with management authority in Korea, it must file a business registration application with the district NTS tax office having jurisdiction over that domestic place of business. The application is made in person or through a tax representative and requires: (i) foreign certificate of incorporation and articles of association authenticated or apostilled; (ii) evidence of the domestic place of business (lease agreement, land registry abstract, or office ownership certificate); (iii) appointment of a domestic chief officer or tax representative with a domestic address and a power of attorney if the foreign corporation has no Korean-resident officer; (iv) passport/ID copies of the authorised representative; and (v) any relevant foreign business/tax registration certificate. If the entity has no Korean domestic place of business but is nonetheless liable for Korean VAT on supplies to Korea, NTS provides a HomeTax foreign-business registration path in which the foreign taxpayer supplies its home-country tax identification number, foreign address, and representative details and receives a Korean VAT identification number. Once registered, NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number, which functions as the Korean TIN and VAT ID, and the taxpayer must activate electronic tax-invoice issuance, e-filing credentials, and foreign currency receipt reporting through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not apply a US-style check-the-box election or permit pass-through classification for a Chusik Hoesa. A domestic stock corporation is always a separate corporate tax resident subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act apply separately and do not provide elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold in KRW: VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of business for every person engaged in a supply of goods or services, including foreign non-resident entities with a domestic place of business and foreign businesses supplying qualifying electronic or digital services to Korean customers. Simplified VAT-filing mechanics are available for small businesses with prior-year supplies below KRW 80 million, but the registration threshold remains zero.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax-invoice (e-tax invoice) system through the HomeTax portal. For every VAT-taxable supply, the supplier must issue a tax invoice and transmit the electronic tax invoice to NTS by the end of the day following invoice issuance, using HomeTax online filing, EDI, or an approved e-invoice service-provider API. There is no real-time fiscal pre-clearance or government digital stamp requirement; fraud prevention is achieved by automated cross-matching of issued/received e-invoices with VAT returns, customs export declarations, and foreign-exchange settlement data, plus system-generated unique invoice sequences and mandatory taxpayer authentication.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Korean VAT law is available for exported goods and for services supplied to, used in, or consumed in a foreign country, including international maritime towage and salvage engagement by a Korean marine operator. The service must be rendered pursuant to a contract with a foreign counterparty, the place of performance must be outside Korea or in international waters, and the consideration must be invoiced to and settled from the foreign party in foreign currency. For deep-sea towage and salvage, a normal commercial contract such as Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement or an international towage contract supports zero-rating only if complete documentary proof of export performance and foreign exchange earning is maintained. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-resident customers are also zero-rated when effectively used or consumed outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export clearance report accepted through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic system, including the declaration number and export approval date)
Marine Bill of Lading, sea waybill, or equivalent ocean-transport document for towed equipment, vessels, and salvage service performance
Salvage or towage contract (Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement, SCOPIC evidence, or international towage hire agreement) identifying the foreign principal and currency of remuneration
Commercial invoice and itemised salvage/towage remuneration statement (statement of account and final disbursements)

Inward Remittance Certificate (Foreign Exchange Receipt/Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank) evidencing actual receipt of the salvage or towage consideration in foreign currency
Master's service report or salvage service performance report (narrative, location of salvage, casualty log, towage route, and time of service)
Certificate of vessel registration or classification and international voyage evidence for the tug or salvage vessel
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is available only where the goods or services are physically exported or rendered abroad and the foreign exchange is properly repatriated within the statutory export settlement period. If the prescribed evidence is missing, the service is diverted to domestic use, or the foreign-exchange proceeds are not received or repatriated within the deadline, the tax authorities recharacterise the supply as a taxable domestic service and assess VAT at 10%, with statutory additional tax and overdue interest. False invoices, fictitious export declarations, or fraudulent use of export certificates are treated as tax evasion: the VAT credit or refund is clawed back retrospectively, the taxpayer is liable for the underpaid VAT plus surcharges and daily overdue penalties, and the prosecutor may impose criminal penalties (fines and imprisonment) under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The ordinary five-year VAT reassessment period applies to honest-error cases; in cases involving false documentation or fraudulent foreign-exchange schemes, Korean authorities may pursue investigation without the benefit of a shortened limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), operating in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the primary foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) as supervisory coordinator; day-to-day foreign exchange business is executed exclusively through licensed foreign exchange banks in South Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberal but notification-heavy foreign exchange regime. Current-account transactions, including invoicing for offshore towage and salvage services, are generally free and convertible, subject to submission of supporting contract evidence to a designated foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa, are permitted but require pre-registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act via the ROK government Invest KOREA portal, followed by issuance of a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (for large or review-worthy amounts) or filing confirmation with the chosen foreign exchange bank. KRW is convertible to foreign currency for bona fide trade and service payments, but banks must verify underlying documentation and customer purpose codes. The key practical hurdles are documentation-heavy remittance procedures, anti-money laundering checks on the beneficial owner, strict beneficial ownership disclosure to banks under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act, and the need to demonstrate that the salvage or towage contract is economically real and not a disguised capital movement. Profit remittance is permitted after tax clearance and after presenting annual audited financial statements or a certified public accountant confirmation, but the remittance is treated as a dividend subject to Corporate Tax Act withholding in the absence of a tax treaty benefit. Foreign currency deposits may be held in domestic foreign currency accounts without mandatory conversion to KRW, but any conversion must be priced at market and reported through the bank. Overall, current-account convertibility is high, while capital-account flows require structured documentation, bank approvals, and post-transaction reporting to the Bank of Korea through the bank's foreign exchange information system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current Foreign Exchange Transaction Framework, South Korea has no mandatory percentage surrender requirement for export service proceeds; a domestic entity may retain up to 100% of foreign currency receipts in a foreign exchange deposit account held with a licensed foreign exchange bank. The statutory discipline is procedural rather than conversion-based: proceeds from cross-border maritime services must be collected through an officially designated foreign exchange bank, must be reconciled against the underlying towage or salvage contract and invoice, and the bank must record the receipt in the Foreign Exchange Information System within the reporting cycle prescribed by MOEF regulations. In practice, foreign currency receipts from service exports must enter the Korean banking system; they cannot settle through unlicensed offshore digital payment intermediaries. There is no fixed statutory export surrender timeline for service income under the current law, but the underlying salvage or towage contract should state a commercial payment due date, and the bank will require the entity to submit evidence of collection status for annual foreign exchange audits. If the proceeds are received from a jurisdiction with restricted settlement, the bank may require a dual-use letter of credit or an independent payment undertaking from a correspondent bank. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero; however, any conversion to KRW, or any use of those foreign currency funds for payments to third parties, will be treated as a foreign exchange transaction requiring appropriate purpose codes and source documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / FX Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Trade Settlement Account for Maritime Infrastructure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions are not viable as a primary banking rail for a resident Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only foreign exchange banks licensed by the MOEF and authorized by the Bank of Korea may conduct foreign exchange business with Korean residents. Unlicensed offshore EMIs, including digital wallet providers and non-bank payment institutions, are legally barred from opening KRW-denominated accounts, collecting service export proceeds on behalf of a Korean resident entity, or executing outward remittances in KRW. An offshore EMI may be used only for non-KRW, third-country receivables in jurisdictions where the Korean entity maintains a separate operational presence, but this is ancillary and cannot replace a domestic corporate account. Any attempt to route salvage or towage payments through an unlicensed EMI will be rejected by Korean banks and may trigger adverse foreign exchange violation findings, monetary penalties, and a freeze on existing banking relationships. The compliance stance is that the Korean entity must onboard with at least one Tier-1 domestic commercial bank, with SWIFT connectivity, and any overseas settlement must be cleared through licensed correspondent banking channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, the statutory representative and the authorized controller are generally required to appear for an in-person KYC interview at a Korean branch during the initial account opening, particularly when opening a foreign currency account or a capital escrow account. Remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly permitted in Korea: while some banks accept notarized and apostilled powers of attorney from foreign directors, they still mandate at least one senior director or the appointed Korean company representative with an Alien Registration Card to attend an in-person identity verification session under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act. For expedited onboarding, the recommended protocol is for the CEO or CFO, holding a valid Korean visa or Alien Registration Card, to visit the bank with the original Certificate of Corporate Seal, a certified copy of the company registration registered with the Korean court, the Foreign Investment Reporting Certificate, and a board resolution designating transaction signatures. The bank will also require proof of the ultimate beneficial owner's identity and residence; for offshore owners, a notarized and apostilled passport copy, reference letter from a recognized foreign bank, and a current corporate extract from the home registry are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime salvage and towage contracts frequently involve time-sensitive emergency services, incomplete documentation, and jurisdiction ambiguity around the location of the casualty, making it difficult for the bank to establish the true commercial substance and the territorial source of the transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a fully executed Lloyds Open Form salvage contract or a standard BIMCO Towcon/Towhire agreement, geolocation coordinates and vessel movement records from AIS/VDR, contemporaneous incident reports, a notarized master's log extract, class society confirmation of vessel condition, the P&I club letter confirming the casualty, and a written jurisdictional note confirming whether the service occurred in or outside Korean territorial waters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chains, offshore nominee shareholders, or flag-of-convenience vessels associated with the contracting counterparty are a standard red flag in Korean banking AML screening and could trigger enhanced due diligence, refusal of the account, or a filing to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete beneficial ownership map from each shareholder through to the ultimate individual controller with supporting registry extracts, apostilled certificates of incumbency for any holdings company, notarized copies of passports for all individuals with 10% or more interest, a corporate structure chart sealed by the representative director, and a notarized board resolution approving the Korean entity incorporation and designated bank signatures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The towage or salvage counterparty could be a shipowner or cargo interest on a sanctions list, or the casualty may be in a territorial sea subject to UN, OFAC, EU, or U.S. Department of Treasury sanctions, creating an unacceptable sanctions nexus for the bank's clearing operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a comprehensive transactional sanctions and adverse-media clearance report generated within five business days of account opening, including UN Sanctions List, OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UK OFSI, and Korean FSS sanctions screening results for the vessel, owner, charterer, managers, insurers, cargo interests, and ultimate counterparty; also provide the casualty's vessel flag, class certificate, charter party, current crew list, cargo manifest, and an independent compliance opinion confirming the absence of a prohibited sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests to route settlements to third-party escrow accounts, purported government maritime authorities, or insurance intermediaries rather than to the original contracting vessel owner can indicate financial crime risk or undocumented service fees, and Korean banks often reject such arrangements at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the original escrow agreement executed between the Korean entity, the foreign maritime claimant, and the escrow agent, along with the licensed banking or legal identity of the escrow agent, a schedule of disbursement flows, the equalized invoice supporting each fee line, the relevant SWIFT allocation instructions, a purpose code breakdown, and a signed declaration from the Korean CFO stating that the routing was adopted for casualty security reasons and that no undisclosed beneficiaries exist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection into the Chusik Hoesa must occur through a designated foreign exchange bank after the foreign investor submits a Foreign Investment Registration Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The recommended routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate foreign shareholder's bank to the Korean entity's capital escrow account at a Tier-1 Korean bank, with the note field containing the foreign investment registration number, the investor's name, the investee Corporate Registration Number, and the Korean Foreign Exchange transaction purpose code for foreign direct investment, typically classified under 'Foreign Investment Under FIPA'. The bank will perform a capital verification by matching the incoming MT103, the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate or confirmation, the board resolution approving the capital issue, and the contribution schedule. A foreign exchange bank confirmation of receipt is then filed electronically by the bank; the company must register the capital increase with the Korean court within statutory corporate timelines. No conversion to KRW is required unless the company needs to pay local expenses; if conversion occurs, the bank will debit the foreign currency account and credit the KRW operating account at the prevailing rate, generating a foreign exchange transaction confirmation that must be retained for audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for tug hire, salvage awards, bunker payments, repair dock payments, crew payroll, and emergency disbursements should be executed over SWIFT MT103, directly instructed by the Chusik Hoesa's treasury operations to any licensed Korean bank. Letters of credit are appropriate only when international rescue or towage contracts require security from a shipowner's bank; the standard instrument is an irrevocable standby letter of credit or a commercial letter of credit issued via SWIFT MT700, with a corresponding MT710 confirmation in the case of a confirming third-country bank. Documentary collections, while legally permissible through SWIFT MT400-based instructions, are disfavored for time-critical salvage because salvage payments are often conditioned on the completion of the rescue and the release of security; an escrow-based payment structure using a Bank Payment Undertaking or a formal escrow agreement held at a Korean 'foreign exchange bank' is the preferred rail for multi-currency settlement. All outgoing payments must carry the statutory foreign exchange purpose code, a full economic justifications package, invoice references, and, when applicable, a certificate of withholding tax settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won-U.S. dollar deliverable forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the value of confirmed towage or salvage receivables or payables under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) executed with a Korean Bank settlement branch and reflecting an eligible hedged exposure, in accordance with Bank of Korea market guidance and the requirement that the contract not be entered on a speculative basis

Cross-currency swap contracts between KRW and USD or EUR for matching the foreign currency debt service and longer-duration salvage contract receivables, subject to bank approval and underlying exposure documentation

Currency basis swaps and rolling FX forwards used strictly to align vessel operating cost payments and salvage security collections to the corporate treasury cash flow cycle, with no prohibited speculative leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and approval of annual financial statements, including presentation of the statutory auditor's report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; corporate registered office records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; if audited companies elect the extended financial statement settlement, the AGM must still be held before the extended corporate tax return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the AGM within the statutory period are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,500) under the Korean Commercial Act; continued failure to approve and maintain financial statements may lead to judicial dissolution proceedings, civil liability of directors, and suspension of tax filing benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and supporting audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: March 31 of the following year under the standard filing rule; if the company is subject to mandatory external audit, the filing deadline is extended by one month to April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the corporate tax due (increasing to 30% if the tax is unfiled for more than six months), statutory interest on unpaid tax at 3.5% per annum, plus a 10% unfaithful tax report penalty; persistent noncompliance triggers compulsory collection, seizure of corporate assets, director personal liability for wilful nonpayment, and potential judicial dissolution upon petition; Korea does not have an administrative strike-off but the court may order a dormant company to be dissolved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax (surtax on corporate income) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local autonomous government (Gu office or Si/Gun office having jurisdiction over the registered head office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the corporate income tax return; for a December 31 year-end, March 31 (or April 30 if an audited company uses the extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid local income tax, daily overdue interest at the statutory rate, and local administrative disposition including attachment or forced collection; persistent nonpayment can result in the sale of corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report submission and public disclosure (only for companies above the statutory audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system; a copy must be delivered to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) and to the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the date of the AGM at the latest; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the audit report must be completed and filed before the AGM (typically by March 31, or by April 30 if the audited company claims the one-month tax extension) and must accompany the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of audit reporting obligations under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies is punishable by administrative fines up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 15,000); the Financial Services Commission may also designate an external auditor, nullify the corporate tax filing extension, and refer criminal misconduct to the prosecutors for severe noncompliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO and shareholding change confirmation for financial institution due diligence (annual when requested); foreign investor reporting when shareholding changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial institutions carry out enhanced due diligence; foreign exchange banks or the Ministry of Economy and Finance (for reportable foreign exchange transactions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For ordinary private companies, no fixed annual UBO government filing is required; beneficial ownership data must be confirmed annually during banking and AML re-kyc procedures; any non-resident acquisition of 10% or more of shares must be reported to a foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate shareholder and beneficial ownership records can trigger FIU fines and administrative sanctions under anti-money laundering legislation; wilful omission or false entry in the shareholder register is a criminal offence under the Commercial Act, punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment or fines up to KRW 50 million.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In South Korea, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies ('External Audit Act') for (i) every stock company (Chusik Hoesa) whose total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million) at the end of the relevant fiscal year; (ii) all companies listed on a Korean securities exchange (KOSPI, KOSDAQ, KONEX) irrespective of asset size; (iii) financial institutions, insurance companies, securities companies and other regulated financial entities regardless of turnover; and (iv) any company that the Financial Services Commission designates as being of significant public interest or where investor protection necessitates an audit. No employee headcount threshold applies; the decisive quantitative triggers are asset size, listing status, or an FSC designation. A company falling below the asset threshold may still be required to undergo an audit if it voluntarily opts to do so under its articles or loan covenants. Any audited company must prepare its financial statements under K-IFRS (Korea International Financial Reporting Standards), fully converged with IFRS, and must engage an external auditor registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korea International Financial Reporting Standards) for all mandatory external audit companies; Korean SMEs may apply the Korean SMEs General Accounting Framework (K-SME GAAP), but only if below the audit threshold and not listed; the statutory books and underlying vouchers must be prepared in accordance with the Commercial Act and the External Audit Act, using the accrual basis and double-entry bookkeeping.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a centralised annual UBO registry filing for ordinary private stock companies. Instead, the Commercial Act requires every Chusik Hoesa to maintain a comprehensive Register of Shareholders (jujumyeongbu) at its registered office, and each transfer of shares must be recorded in that register before the transfer can be asserted against the company. Directors are required to update the register accurately without undue delay; a transfer that is not registered has no corporate effect. For AML/CFT purposes, every company must internally identify its ultimate beneficial owners, and financial institutions will require annual confirmation of UBO information as part of customer due diligence. Separately, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any non-resident's acquisition of 10% or more of a Korean company's shares, or any subsequent change in holdings, must be reported to a foreign exchange bank or designated authority within 30 days. There is no federal '30-day' UBO reporting obligation for purely domestic shareholders, but the company secretary must process all share transfer documentation and update the register within the statutory corporate-governance timeframe.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – 2,500 per annum in Seoul metropolitan area; USD 500 – 1,800 per annum in regional provinces, inclusive of registered address, corporate secretarial administration, statutory register custody and compliance monitoring
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 – 25,000 per annum for a mandatory certified audit of a medium-sized Chusik Hoesa engaged in offshore towage and maritime salvage; USD 2,000 – 5,000 for voluntary compilation or review services if the entity is below the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10%–25% progressive national corporate income tax: 10% on tax base up to KRW 200 million, 20% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 22% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 25% above KRW 300 billion; plus a 10% local income tax surtax producing an aggregate headline range of 11%–27.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-tech enterprises and entities in the Incheon Free Economic Zone or other designated Free Economic Zones may enjoy a 50%–100% exemption or reduction of corporate tax for up to 5 years, subject to investment scale and business substance; technology transfer and patent-type income may qualify for reduced tax or 50% income deduction under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; R&D and facility investment tax credits are also available. For offshore towage and salvage, the taxpayer must prove actual employment, vessel ownership or bareboat charter, onboard crew management and emergency-response capability in Korea, because a letterhead-only free-zone registration will not reduce tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 12, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (Corporate Tax Return), filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal; mandatory electronic filing for corporations with total assets equal to or greater than KRW 10 billion.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end under Corporate Tax Act Article 60; an extension of up to 1 month is available where security or an approved accountant is designated, and a longer extension may apply for subsidiaries with a foreign parent whose audit calendar requires it. The return must be submitted to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the Chusik Hoesa's head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification: legal name, registration number, representative director, head office address, tax office code, fiscal year-end and principal business code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Chusik Hoesa legal name and Korean registration number. If a non-resident owns the shares, identify the ultimate beneficial owner in the supplementary shareholders register; failure to match the bank/escrow account with the declared legal name is an automatic audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business type and place of business: towage fleets, tugboat registration, salvage contracts, insurance certificates and any foreign establishments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every foreign branch, PE or booking center that receives Lloyd's Standard Form wires. Korea taxes worldwide income of domestic corporations, so profits allocated to a foreign branch must be proven by treaty permanent establishment thresholds and by the transfer-pricing file; a foreign bank account without board authorization is a shell-company indicator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting standard and financial statement reference: K-IFRS or generally accepted accounting principles, audited statements, and fiscal-year alignment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the Korean audited statements are translated into Korean/English as required and reconciled to the overseas group statements. Any difference in revenue recognition for salvage rewards must be explained in the tax reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and deductible expenses: gross revenue from ocean towage, salvage rewards, Lloyd's Open Form settlements, insurance proceeds, demurrage, and all operating costs including fuel, crew wages, insurance premiums, port dues and subcontract towage fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize salvage and towage revenue in the taxable year in which the right to receive the income becomes fixed, using the Bank of Korea certified exchange rate. Every wire from Lloyd's or an escrow agent must be traceable to a contract; unreconciled escrow receipts will be assessed as omitted income for the non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation adjustments: non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation adjustments, capital versus revenue classification, bad debts, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible payments to non-resident affiliates lacking economic substance, fines for maritime pollution, and unverified entertainment expenses. The branch or shareholder must attach certified foreign tax returns for any foreign tax credit claim on towage income taxed abroad; credit cannot exceed Korean tax attributable to that income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable: taxable base, progressive rate calculation, local income tax surtax, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10/20/22/25% brackets, add 10% local income tax surtax, then subtract foreign tax credits and interim prepayments. If a shareholder is a non-resident, the dividend distribution and related withholding liability must be reflected in the accompanying schedules; underwithholding leaves the Korean company liable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder and distribution declaration: dividends, deemed dividends, deemed capital distributions, and profit-reserve movements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare dividends to non-resident shareholders on the non-resident withholding schedule, and remit the withholding tax by the statutory due date. If no dividend is declared, be prepared to justify retained earnings against business expansion and tugboat replacement; excessive retention in a cash-skinny salvage company is a tax-reform red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Representative declaration, related-party transaction disclosure, foreign account declaration, and electronic signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The representative director, even if a nominee for a foreign owner, must sign the declaration. If foreign-related party transactions exceed the statutory threshold, attach the statement of domestic transactions with foreign related parties and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documents; a non-resident director cannot rely on ignorance of Korean tax consequences.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate tax return attracts an unfaithful tax-filing penalty of 20% of the underreported taxable income if the return is negligent, 30% where gross negligence has caused omission, and 40% where false or fraudulent documents are used; a zero-tax return filed late carries an administrative fine of KRW 200,000, and unpaid taxes attract daily late-payment interest at approximately 8% per annum. Where intentional evasion exceeds KRW 300 million, criminal referral under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act can lead to imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to five times the evaded tax; the tax authority may also blacklist the entity and representative for three years, blocking public procurement and maritime licenses.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate on outbound dividends (20% national dividend withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax), unless reduced by a bilateral double tax treaty. Treaty rates often range from 5% to 15% depending on shareholding thresholds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence covering the year of payment, complete and file with the Korean withholding agent or the National Tax Service the Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Withholding Tax under the Tax Treaty, and provide a Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming that the recipient is the ultimate owner and not a conduit for another person or a third-country national. The substantive document package must include board minutes, audited accounts, employment records, a business licence, and bank evidence showing real economic activity in the residence state. If the treaty application is not accepted before payment, the Korean payer must withhold the 22% statutory rate and the recipient may file a refund claim within the five-year statutory period; the tax authority will deny treaty benefits where the recipient has no substance and the sole purpose is treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% aggregate (20% plus 2% local surtax). Under the applicable DTA, interest commonly may be reduced to 10% or exempt for financial institutions in certain treaties, and royalties are commonly reduced to 2%–15% depending on the type of intellectual property and whether the royalty is paid for the right to use industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment; the beneficial ownership and permanent establishment conditions must still be satisfied for the reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 in aggregate foreign-related-party transactions for the taxable year triggers the contemporaneous Statement of Transactions with Foreign Related Parties and the Local File; Master File is required when consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and foreign-related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion, and Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with annual consolidated revenue of at least KRW 700 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the offshore ESR regime, but economic substance is enforced through substance-over-form, the anti-conduit provisions of the Korea-U.S. and similar DTAs, and the specific foreign corporation deemed-income rules of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. For an offshore towage and salvage Chusik Hoesa, Core Income-Generating Activities must include tugboat chartering negotiation, salvage command, crew supervision, safety and emergency-response coordination, invoicing and bank account control in Korea; if those functions are performed from a head office in another jurisdiction, profits must be allocated accordingly and transfer-pricing returns must reflect the true value-creation locations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Bank Protocol Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Lloyd's Standard Form wire settlements and salvage-reward escrow receipts from gross revenue in Box 4, splitting large towage invoices among multiple foreign bank accounts to stay below audit thresholds, using another company's vessel registration to disguise revenue, or submitting fabricated voyage logs to support a zero or loss return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 66 and 76, and Tax Evasion Punishment Act Article 3: additional tax equal to 40% of omitted tax plus daily late-payment interest, criminal fine up to five times the evaded tax, and imprisonment up to 7 years; the tax authority can blacklist the corporation and representative for three years and revoke the maritime towage/salvage licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who signs false returns is personally secondarily liable under National Tax Collection Act Article 10 where corporate assets are insufficient; the director's personal bank accounts and vessels can be seized, the director is placed on the National Tax Service travel-ban list, and criminal conviction for evasion exceeding KRW 300 million carries a mandatory minimum imprisonment term; civil restitution claims by minority shareholders and creditors can pierce the corporate veil on alter-ego grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Intercompany Transfer Pricing and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an offshore sister tugboat company below-market salvage rates, routing Lloyds Open Form settlements to a related shell entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction, or paying inflated management, insurance, or escrow-service fees to a non-resident affiliate that has no employees or assets in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Articles 4 and 6: the tax authority re-computes taxable income under the arm's-length principle and imposes a 20% unfaithful-return penalty and tax interest; failure to produce contemporaneous documentation can expose a KRW 20 million to KRW 150 million administrative fine, denial of the refund statute protection, and criminal punishment where false invoices are used to disguise the transfer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are joint tortfeasors with the company where they sign false transfer-pricing documentation or order the destruction of vessel charter records; Korean courts will pierce the corporate veil where the director commingles personal escrow accounts, uses the offshore affiliate as a conduit, or abandons corporate formalities, thereby imposing personal liability for the reassessed tax, interest, penalties, and litigation costs; the director may also be personally investigated for fraud and prohibited from leaving Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Fraud and Abusive Treaty Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the statutory 22% aggregate rate, claiming a treaty-reduced rate without a valid Tax Residency Certificate, or appointing a shareholder in a low-tax jurisdiction as a nominee with the actual economic benefit passing to a Korean resident director.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 97 and 98 and Tax Evasion Punishment Act Article 11: the Korean payer is liable for the unwithheld tax, a 10% negligent penalty or 40% fraudulent penalty[feasible], daily late-payment interest, and may be denied the business-expense deduction for the royalty or interest payment; a false treaty application is a separate offence subject to criminal fine and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and any director who controls the withholding function are jointly and severally liable to remit the withheld tax; where the director personally receives the offshore dividend or royalty as the true beneficial owner, the corporate form is disregarded and the director becomes the direct taxpayer; sanctions include civil restitution of the evaded amounts, asset seizure, blacklisting as an irresponsible businessman for up to six years, and criminal imprisonment for tax fraud and false public records.
